auditor.independence_note: This session wrote no fr value and edited no catalogue, context sidecar, script or ledger. Every judgement is derived from the bytes on disk — en plus its .context.json sidecar against fr — and from the shipped fr catalogue outside these eleven namespaces. The s3a/s3b/s3c receipts were used only as a checklist of findings to verify, never as evidence of what the bytes say. The repository is untouched apart from this receipt.

verdict_reason: All 11 namespaces whose bytes changed since the s3c receipt were audited in full on the final bytes; the other 10 of the 21 were carried on hash evidence, not assumption. No BLOCKER and no MAJOR: the s3c MAJOR (device_move D1, « cet appareil » where the English says the destination device) is applied and closed as « cet appareil-là », and all 22 prior findings are accounted for — 21 applied as proposed (of which K1's value matches its proposal but still reads awkwardly, recorded as the non-gating NIT below), and 1 (R2) deliberately deferred because the finding itself placed its fix in a follow-on slice. New findings are 2 MINOR and 3 NIT, with 4 INFO observations recorded rather than churned. The two MINORs: one typography/consistency miss (the colon in session_readout.access.device_bound.title carries a plain ASCII space where this locale uses U+202F in 557 shipped places, in five sibling lines of the same popover, and where this same round used U+202F in session_spend.summary.total and composer_notes.default_not_saved), and one glossary residue (stalled is « interrompu » here and « en attente » in the shipped ui.chat.pickers.destination_pickers.stalled_send_a_message_to_continue). Structurally the eleven namespaces are clean: 158 ICU argument headers inspected with zero non-ASCII whitespace inside a header, zero non-ASCII inside a ::keyword, every argument name and number skeleton identical to English, one/many/other present wherever French needs it, and every key rendered through intl-messageformat at 0/1/2/5/11/21/100 plus 1 000 000 — 0 and 1 correctly take the French singular, and the many branch fires only at 10^6 as CLDR French requires.

limits: Per-key diff of what the translator changed is NOT reconstructable: the eleven fr catalogue files are untracked in this worktree (git status shows them as ??), so no pre-remediation blob exists to diff against, and the s3c receipt recorded hashes rather than values. Each of the eleven was therefore audited in full on the final bytes, which is the stronger check; the cost is that a judgement here cannot say 'this key was untouched by the remediation'.

Width and overflow are judged from character counts and from rendered strings, not from a live frame. session_readout.access.device_bound.title (45 vs 30 characters), ask_queue.expiry.now_short (« imminent » vs « now ») and the rail chip's waiting clause are the strings a rendered check should confirm; none of them is claimed to overflow.
Only fr was opened. The other six locales were not read, and no cross-locale consistency claim is made.
node scripts/i18n/generate.mjs --check was not run: the generated catalogue is stale until the manager regenerates, so its result would not be evidence about these bytes.

Rhythm, sentence length and screen-reader order were judged by reading the rendered strings, not by listening to a screen reader; the two screen-reader-only strings (composer_notes.outside_mentions, session_readout.strip.effort_aria) were checked for placeholder and plural integrity only.

findings.reason: Glossary: C2 is applied as proposed, taking its « interrompu » option, so this slice is internally consistent — but the locale now carries TWO French spellings of the English term `stalled`: « interrompu » in these four keys and « en attente » in the shipped ui.chat.pickers.destination_pickers.stalled_send_a_message_to_continue (English « stalled — send a message to continue »). The drift C2 named has therefore moved rather than closed. The value here is the better French for a goal that stopped mid-flight (« en attente » already means pending/waiting in this slice, e.g. ui.chat.asks.outstanding_aria), so the recommendation is to keep these four and re-word the shipped picker key in a follow-on slice that owns it, not to churn this round.

findings.reason: Typography/consistency: R1 is applied exactly as its proposed value was written, and that value carries a PLAIN ASCII space (U+0020) before the colon — verified in the bytes, not by eye: the character at index of ':' is 0x20, and the file contains no U+202F there. The locale's own convention is the narrow no-break space: across all shipped fr catalogues, prose ':' is preceded by U+202F 557 times, by U+00A0 once, and by a plain space 11 times (the 11 are pre-existing, in ui.chat.asks, ui.chat.usage_reset, ui.hub.links, ui.notifications and ui.settings). Five sibling lines in the same popover already use U+202F (access.history.grant_expiry, last_checked, last_resolved, draft.confirm_model_effort, strip.effort_aria), and this same remediation round used U+202F before ':' in ui.chat.session_spend.summary.total and before ';' in ui.chat.ask_answer.moved_on — so this one key is the odd one out in its own round. The proposed value above is identical in wording; the change is the single character before the colon, from U+0020 to U+202F. No rendering risk either way (it is one glyph narrower), which is why this is a MINOR of consistency rather than a defect that breaks a frame.

R2 is not applied by design: it recorded that with the fallback filling {owner} the title begins with a lowercase article (« l’appareil propriétaire ne peut pas fournir l’accès »), and that the fix belongs in the follow-on slice that owns access.owner_fallback, because that fallback must stay lowercase where it is used mid-sentence (« auprès de {owner} », « via {owner} »). The reason stands and the fallback key is byte-unchanged, so this is correctly deferred rather than dropped.

Verified-OK against the sidecar note « Keep the x prefix; it reads as 'extra high' ». The prefix is dropped, which is the right call in French — « xÉlevé » is not a French form — and « Très élevé » conveys extra-high next to the untranslated « Max » and the identical « Minimal ». Recorded as an observation so the sidecar instruction is visibly considered rather than missed, not as a defect.

findings.reason: Idiom/agreement: the count is moved behind a colon and the feminine plural « expirées » is left without a noun to agree with, so the rendered chip reads « 1 question en attente · expirées : 2 » — a dangling participle in label position.
